To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the visual attention problem can be solved by a hierarchy of winner take-all processes that are embedded in the visual processing network, that this solution is highly compatible with neurobiological evidence and that this model is superior to other computational solutions for the problem of visual attention.
the visual processing network is selectively tuned by a winner take all process and this process is the basis of visual attention.
attention is a top down process, that the top down process is a winner take all mechanism, that this process operates in a hierarchical fashion, and that the process is selective.

modeling visual attention and its role in visual perception.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the model provides a solution for the problems of selection, information routing and task specific attention in a hierarchical visual system and that it provides a solution to the problem of vision that is biologically plausible and computationally effective.
selective tuning is an effective solution to the problem of visual attention.
this model is a significant step towards an understanding of the mechanisms underlying visual attention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this model of selective tuning is a viable computational solution for the problem of visual attention in a robot or machine vision system.
we have provided a computational solution to the problem of visual attention that is biologically plausible, computationally efficient, and highly appropriate to the problem in machine vision.

we have developed a computational model for attention which has the following features: (1) It provides for a selection of image regions based on a combination of bottom up and top down processes; (2) The model provides for a mechanism to route information to higher levels of processing; and (3) The model provides a mechanism for attentional biasing which is task specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that
attention can be implemented as a top down winner take all mechanism.
a model based on selective tuning provides a unified solution to the problem of visual attention in both biological and machine vision.

the visual processing hierarchy is a natural substrate for implementing attention and is not something that needs to be added to the visual processing network as is the case with other models of attention.
